chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: The Dreamland Cafe at Fourth and Central, 1921
summary: Spikes opened the Dreamland nightclub in 1921 with Kid Ory's band, later Black and Tan under Harry Southard, and singers Rucker and Carolyn Williams.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: What...during that period, what...where else was music heard? I mean, were there clubs on Central Avenue--or where were the clubs? Well, you opened a place around...
I had three places on Central Avenue. The first one was the Dreamland.

Nightclub at Fourth and Central. Yeah, that's where Kid Ory and them was playing, and when I closed that, I built a place in Watts was called the Watts Country Club, and then I come in town later on and opened the Jockey Club, the one I showed you, you know, the card of. And then Mosby closed up the Alabam, and then Will Heflin and I opened that up a little later on.
What years for all of these? Do you know the years? First, the Dreamland? What year did you open the Dreamland?
And you had music in there?
Yeah, I had the band, and I had...
That was where Ory played, right?

Yeah, and I had...uh, Black and Tan played there, and I had two...three entertainers--Rucker, and I had...oh, I can't think of...Carolyn Sn...Carolyn Williams. She was great at that time, you know --floor singer. And I had a couple of other singers.
And Black and Tan was led by Paul Howard, wasn't it?
No. Harry Southard was supposed to be the leader and manager.
I see. Paul Howard was just in the band.
He was in the band. Yeah. After Mutt 'n' left 'n' them--we had a little disagreement and they left--then I put the hot ...I put the Black and Tan in there.
And the next...how long did you have the Dreamland?
